title: They smiled in public.
paragraphs:
They smiled in public.
But bowed in private.
And nobody saw it at first.

Because compromise rarely announces itself.
It whispers.
It negotiates.
It waits until conviction dies quietly in the background.

Jehoiada stood in a generation where truth was negotiable, where leaders wore the garments of God but feared the opinions of men. And somewhere in that same nation, there were people who still showed up to worship…
…but their hearts had already made deals in the dark.
Here’s the tension you can’t ignore:
How do you live right in front of a godly influence… but fall apart when they’re gone?

How do you sing loud on Sabbath…
but stay silent when sin knocks on your private door?
Jehoiada didn’t just fight a wicked queen.
He stood in the middle of a people who had learned how to look faithful without being faithful.
And that’s where this stops being their story…
Because some of us don’t have a rebellion problem.
We have a hidden compromise problem.

You still pray.
Still post verses.
Still show up.
But there’s a quiet negotiation happening in your heart.

A sin you’ve renamed.
A habit you’ve justified.
A conviction you’ve slowly lowered.
One small compromise at a time.
One “it’s not that bad” at a time.

Until holiness became optional…
and obedience became conditional.
That’s exactly what happened after Jehoiada.
While he lived, King Joash walked straight.

But when the voice of conviction disappeared…
the king revealed what was really in his heart.

“Now after the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and paid homage to the king, and the king listened to them… They abandoned the house of the Lord…”
— 2 Chronicles 24:17–18
They didn’t lose access to God.
They lost their hunger for Him.
Some scholars interpret this as proof that Joash’s faith was never truly rooted—only influenced. Not transformed. Not owned.
Borrowed faith will collapse under pressure.

If your conviction only lives when you're around strong believers…
it’s not conviction.

There are areas in your life where you know the truth…
but you’re still negotiating with sin.

But you’re asking,
“Did He really mean it like that?”
That’s compromise wearing a polite face.
Because sin doesn’t need to destroy you overnight.
It just needs to slowly own you quietly.

“Then desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin when it is fully grown brings forth death.”
— James 1:15

Until what once bothered you…
no longer even convicts you.
That’s the scariest place to be—
But when you stop feeling it.
Because Jehoiada’s story doesn’t just expose compromise—
It points to the One who never compromised.

Where Jehoiada stood firm for a season…
Jesus stood firm forever.

In the wilderness—tempted, but unshaken.
In the crowd—pressured, but uncompromised.
On the cross—crushed, but obedient.

“He committed no sin, neither was deceit found in His mouth.”
— 1 Peter 2:22
And here’s the Gospel that changes everything:
You and I are not Jehoiada.

We are the ones who drift.
The ones who compromise.
The ones who look faithful but wrestle secretly.
But Jesus didn’t come for the perfect.

For the ones who smiled in public…
but were breaking in private.
And instead of exposing you to shame—

“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
— Romans 5:8

Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you got consistent.
Not when you became strong.
Not permission to stay the same—
Because Jesus doesn’t just forgive sin.
He doesn’t just clean your record.

“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.”
— 2 Corinthians 5:17
That means you don’t have to live split anymore.

One version of you in public.
Another in private.
You don’t have to keep negotiating with what Jesus already defeated.
But you have to do one thing:
Because repentance is not God shaming you.
What is that one area you’ve been compromising?

Because what you expose to God…
He heals.

But what you hide…
will control you.

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
Don’t just feel convicted for a moment.
And let grace rebuild what sin tried to ruin.
